page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration delivers 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, which yields a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps and does not include local storage or GPU coprocessors.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear architectural tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression are weak, falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% of tested servers respectively. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall within the average middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks also register average performance, though the Passmark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5ne.8xlarge offers a stable resource density of 4 GB RAM per core backed by dedicated physical hardware. However, because its single-threaded performance is weak, it is less cost-efficient for workloads constrained by single-core speed. The instance delivers its best value when running parallelized workloads that can fully utilize the 32 dedicated cores, mitigating the lower single-core efficiency through multi-threaded scaling.

This instance is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations, supported by its average scores in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks using small to medium models, though text generation speeds are modest.
